title: Money then versus now; first New Orleans bands
summary: Handy compares kid earnings with today, then lists playing with Kid Rena, Armstrong and others after arriving in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yes. I tell you what, my mother, I'd go home with 30, 40 dollars and give my mother. And it would seem impossible for us to pick up that kind of money, a piece to go home with. And we have made good money. Made good money. Then I've had cousins and they would likewise. It wasn't three, it was six of us all together. My cousin and I and my brothers. And they'd go around, we called it Surinating and we'd go around Surinating. And we would make, we have made some money during those times. Well, after then, after I came to the city of New Orleans, I played with Kid Quencher, I played with Kid Rainey, I played with Louis Armstrong. During the time he come from Chicago here and he have had our, uh, come down here short of a bass player. Well, I sat in with them. Of course, now I didn't get any money. But I was too glad just to say that I played with the best of, the best of musicians. Then I have worked with our Sydney Dasgene for money.
